record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: Is the Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^3) of degree-d finite subschemes of affine 3-space ever nonreduced for some d?

evidence.quote: Problem I. Is Hilbd(A^3) nonreduced for some d?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3_k)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parametrizing zero-dimensional closed subschemes of length $d$ of affine 3-space $\mathbb{A}^3_k = \mathrm{Spec}\,k[x,y,z]$. Recall that $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3_k)$ represents the functor sending a $k$-scheme $T$ to the set of closed subschemes $Z \subset \mathbb{A}^3_k \times T$ that are finite and flat of degree $d$ over $T$. Determine whether there exists an integer $d \geq 1$ such that the scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3_k)$ is nonreduced; equivalently, decide whether $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3_k)$ is reduced for every $d \geq 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: Reducedness/nonreducedness of the Hilbert scheme of points on affine 3-space remains open. Recent work (Jelisiejew, 2024) exhibits generically nonreduced components of Hilbert schemes of points on smooth varieties of dimension at least 4, but the corresponding question for $\mathbb{A}^3$ is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems including whether Hilb_d(A^3) is ever nonreduced.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Generically nonreduced components of Hilbert schemes on fourfolds
status_evidence.snippet: Nonreduced components are exhibited for Hilbert schemes of points on smooth varieties of dimension at least four.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress resolves the analogous question in dimension >= 4, but not for A^3.

status_evidence.title: Pathologies on the Hilbert scheme of points
status_evidence.snippet: Pathologies are established in higher-dimensional affine spaces, but reducedness of Hilb_d(A^3) is not settled.
status_evidence.claim: The A^3 case remains a notable open question.
